positive_control.requirement: Every case must preserve AIP signature and chain validity so a rejection cannot be explained by credential forgery.
positive_control.expected: The harness reports only the claim-specific constrained result and never upgrades it from an adjacent successful row.

cases.title: Wrong Presenter
cases.expected_permitted_conclusion: The bearer has a valid chain; AIP alone does not establish that the live presenter is the leaf subject.
prohibited_conclusions: The presenter is authenticated as aip:key:agent-a.
AIP failed merely because it accurately declared this limitation.

cases.title: Same-Control Verifier
cases.expected_permitted_conclusion: A named verifier signed the block; AIP draft-01 does not establish organizational independence.
prohibited_conclusions: Different signing keys make the verifier independent.
A Level 2 or Level 3 label proves control-domain separation.

cases.title: Stale/Unverifiable Completion
cases.expected_permitted_conclusion: The signed completion and result hash are intact, but the underlying evidence could not be established as current or checkable.
prohibited_conclusions: Unverifiable evidence was rejected on its merits.
A peer_verified label proves the evidence check succeeded.
A valid completion signature proves the claimed execution occurred correctly.

cases.title: A2A to MCP Action Swap

reused_border_case.mutation: the MCP tool name or its arguments differ from what the authority named
reused_border_case.role: The crossing is where an authority for action X can become an invocation of action Y without either side seeing an anomaly.

cases.expected_permitted_conclusion: The tool remains in AIP scope, but AIP draft-01 does not establish that the observed MCP arguments are the exact payload authorized by the A2A task.
prohibited_conclusions: A valid AIP chain proves the exact cross-protocol payload was authorized.
A matching tool name makes different arguments the same action.
